_comment: Scoring vocabulary for the DailyCoder listener. Tune these freely — listen.py reads this file at runtime, no code change needed. A thread is enqueued when its score >= min_score. Weights are additive; a term counts once no matter how often it appears.

3._why: DailyCoder's actual thesis. Someone worrying out loud that AI is eroding their craft IS the target reader — this is the highest-value thing to reply to, not generic programming chat.

2._why: Direct category adjacency — people already in the market for a small daily practice habit.

1._why: Weak signals. On their own these never clear min_score — they only push a tier-2 or tier-3 hit up the ranking.

_negative_why: Hard excludes. These kill an item outright regardless of score — recruiting spam, course sales, and crypto/AI-tool promos are the three things that reliably pollute these keyword sets.
